rows: SB 1485 (Laws 2021 ch. 359): Permanent Early Voting List renamed Active Early Voting List; a voter is removed after failing to vote an early ballot in all qualifying elections for two consecutive election cycles (after notice)

Shrinks the auto-mailed universe for infrequent early voters from 2023 on; 2022+ 'ballots issued' denominators are not like-for-like with 2016-2020; compare return rates on issued ballots, not raw volume

EAC Policy Survey 2024: no same-day registration; no excuse needed for mail; drop boxes allowed; ballot curing allowed, cure deadline 11/10/2024 (5 days after ED); no postmark rule (ballot must be received by close of polls); in-person early voting 10/09/2024-11/01/2024; drop boxes 10/09/2024-11/05/2024
Receipt-by-ED rule means late mail and 'late early' ballots dropped off on Election Day are counted after election night; Election Day share of the vote was 18.3% in 2022 and 14.3% in 2024 (EAVS)
https://www.eac.gov/research-and-data/datasets-codebooks-and-surveys (2024 Policy Survey, on disk policy2024_core.csv / full CSV)

rows: Arizona Proposition 141, Prohibit Taxes or Fees on Miles Traveled in Motor Vehicle Amendment

Amend the state constitution to prohibit state and local governments from implementing any tax or fee based on vehicle miles traveled and enacting any rule or law to monitor or limit vehicle miles traveled without an individual's consent.[10]
R (revision-pinned Wikipedia table; measure text not opened at the SOS)
Arizona Proposition 142, Prohibit Race- or Ethnicity-Based Preferential Treatment, Public Education Offices, and Disciplinary Policies Amendment

Prohibit the state and government agencies, including public education institutions, from requiring an individual to endorse preferential treatment toward or discrimination against an individual on the basis of race or ethnicity; using public funds to promote or to create or operate an office or position in a public education institution to promote preferential treatment toward or discrimination against a person or group based on their race or ethnicity; or requiring enrollment in a course that promotes the creation of a race-based diversity, equity, and inclusion or intersectionality in modern American society.[11]
R (revision-pinned Wikipedia table; measure text not opened at the SOS)
Arizona Proposition 144, Voter Identification and Citizenship Voting Requirements Amendment

Specify that only citizens may vote in any election in Arizona, prohibit a foreign national from making contributions in an effort to influence an Arizona election, and prohibit others from knowingly accepting such contributions, require voters to provide government-issued identification to cast a ballot, and grant voters the right to have their vote tabulated at their voting location.[12]
R (revision-pinned Wikipedia table; measure text not opened at the SOS)
Arizona Proposition 316, Limit Local Tax Rate on Groceries to 2% of Base Price and Require Voter Approval to Increase Tax Rate Measure
Prohibits local governments from imposing or increasing a tax on the sale of groceries without voter approval and capping the tax rate at 2%.[13]
R (revision-pinned Wikipedia table; measure text not opened at the SOS)
Arizona Proposition 317, Designate Drug Cartels as Terrorist Organizations and Require State DHS to Address Threats Measure
Declares drug cartels to be terrorist organizations and requires the Arizona Department of Homeland Security do "everything within its authority to address the threat posed by drug cartels".[14]
R (revision-pinned Wikipedia table; measure text not opened at the SOS)
Arizona Proposition 318, Require Schools and Athletic Associations to Restrict Use of Restrooms, Locker Rooms, and Other Private Spaces Based on Sex Measure

Prohibit schools and athletic associations from authorizing a student, athlete, employee, or other individual from using a restroom, locker room, shower room, or other private space that is not designated for their sex - with sex defined as the "biological status as male or female as recorded at birth on the individual's original birth certificate;"- and remove the provision allowing any student, including females, to participate in any interscholastic or intramural athletic team or sport designated for males.[15]
R (revision-pinned Wikipedia table; measure text not opened at the SOS)
Arizona Proposition 319, Prohibit New Photo Traffic Enforcement Systems Measure

Prohibit the state, or other government entity, from using photo enforcement systems to identify people who violate certain traffic ordinances, including traffic signs, markings, signals, and speed restrictions.[16]
R (revision-pinned Wikipedia table; measure text not opened at the SOS)
Arizona Proposition 320, Require Certain School Districts to Spend 60% of Operational Spending on Direct Instruction Measure

Require that large school districts (those with more than 7,500 students) spend at least 60% of their budget on direct instructional expenses, and state that the auditor general would be tasked with defining direct instructional expenses.[17]
